```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

**Status.** Figure 1 is *descriptive*. Each plotted point is a model-estimated inoculated-minus-sterile
contrast with an unadjusted 95% CI (**EXPLORATORY**). The only **CONFIRMATORY** test behind the
figure is the three-way interaction `Poly:Inoc:Water` on grain allocation (panel C), reported in
`10_Rigor_Reversal/10_Reversal_Rigor.Rmd`.

The models are the same ones fit in `10_Reversal_Rigor.Rmd`: one full `Poly * Inoc * Water` model
per currency, on all 60 pots, contrasts conditioned inside it. This file re-fits them and then
**checks the plotted numbers against `10_Rigor_Reversal/outputs/reversal_simple_effects.csv`**, so
the figure cannot silently drift from the analysis.

| Panel | Response | Model | Plotted as |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | total NPP per plant | `gls`, `varIdent(~1\|Poly)` (selected in 10, Sec. 2b) | % change |
| B | grain mass per plant | `gls`, equal variance (selected in 10, Sec. 2b) | % change |
| C | grain allocation (**primary**) | beta, `dispformula = ~Poly` (pre-specified) | percentage points |

Sign convention: `Inoc - Strl`, asserted in code. Positive = inoculation increased the response.

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(glmmTMB)
library(nlme)
source("../fig_style.R")   # pal_poly, poly_lab, pal_inoc, facet_poly(), p_label(), theme_fig() ...

wheat <- readRDS("../wheat_audited.rds") %>%
  mutate(log_NPP = log(NPP), log_berry = log(berry))
stopifnot(nrow(wheat) == 60,
          identical(levels(wheat$Inoc), c("Inoc", "Strl")),
          identical(levels(wheat$Water), c("Control", "Moderate", "Severe")))
```

# Models and effect sizes

```{r models}
# weights object spliced into the call (bquote) so emmeans can re-evaluate it; see 10_Reversal_Rigor.Rmd
fit_gls <- function(y, w = NULL) {
  f <- reformulate("Poly*Inoc*Water", y)
  eval(bquote(gls(.(f), weights = .(w), data = wheat, method = "REML")))
}
m_npp   <- fit_gls("log_NPP",   varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Poly))
m_berry <- fit_gls("log_berry")
m_alloc <- glmmTMB(berry_alloc ~ Poly * Inoc * Water, dispformula = ~ Poly,
                   family = beta_family(), data = wheat)

tidy_contrast <- function(model, panel_label, scale = c("log", "response")) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  emm <- emmeans(model, ~ Inoc | Poly * Water, data = wheat)
  if (scale == "response") emm <- regrid(emm)
  # "pairwise" = first level minus second = Inoc - Strl.
  # NOT "revpairwise": with levels (Inoc, Strl) that gives Strl - Inoc and mirrors the figure.
  ct <- contrast(emm, "pairwise", by = c("Poly", "Water"), adjust = "none")
  d  <- as.data.frame(summary(ct, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)))
  stopifnot(all(d$contrast == "Inoc - Strl"))
  lo <- intersect(c("asymp.LCL", "lower.CL"), names(d))[1]
  hi <- intersect(c("asymp.UCL", "upper.CL"), names(d))[1]
  out <- tibble(Poly = d$Poly, Water = d$Water, est = d$estimate, lo = d[[lo]], hi = d[[hi]])
  out <- if (scale == "log") mutate(out, across(c(est, lo, hi), ~ (exp(.x) - 1) * 100))  # % change
         else                mutate(out, across(c(est, lo, hi), ~ .x * 100))             # percentage points
  mutate(out, panel = panel_label)
}

panel_levels <- c("A. Total productivity (NPP)\n% change", "B. Grain mass\n% change", "C. Allocation to grain\npercentage points")
eff <- bind_rows(
  tidy_contrast(m_npp,   panel_levels[1], "log"),
  tidy_contrast(m_berry, panel_levels[2], "log"),
  tidy_contrast(m_alloc, panel_levels[3], "response")
) %>% mutate(panel = factor(panel, panel_levels),
             Poly  = factor(Poly, c("Mono", "Inter")),
             Water = factor(Water, c("Control", "Moderate", "Severe")))

# --- consistency check against the analysis document -------------------------------
chk <- read.csv("../10_Rigor_Reversal/outputs/reversal_simple_effects.csv") %>%
  mutate(panel = case_when(str_starts(currency, "A") ~ panel_levels[1],
                           str_starts(currency, "B") ~ panel_levels[2],
                           str_starts(currency, "C") ~ panel_levels[3]),
         Poly = factor(Poly, c("Mono", "Inter")), Water = factor(Water, c("Control", "Moderate", "Severe"))) %>%
  select(panel, Poly, Water, est_10 = est, lo_10 = lo, hi_10 = hi)
cmp <- eff %>% mutate(panel = as.character(panel)) %>%
  inner_join(chk %>% mutate(panel = as.character(panel)), by = c("panel", "Poly", "Water"))
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == 18,
          max(abs(cmp$est - cmp$est_10), abs(cmp$lo - cmp$lo_10), abs(cmp$hi - cmp$hi_10)) < 1e-6)
cat("Figure estimates match 10_Reversal_Rigor outputs for all 18 contrasts.\n")
```

# Figure 1

```{r figure, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=4.2, dpi=150}
# Figure 1 plots one inoculated-minus-sterile effect per cell, so inoculation is not a plotted
# group here: colour/shape = stand type, using pal_poly / poly_lab from ../fig_style.R.
shp_poly <- c(Mono = 16, Inter = 17)             # shape = second, colour-independent encoding
water_lab_short <- c(Control = "Control", Moderate = "Moderate", Severe = "Severe")
signed <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, paste0("+", x), as.character(x))

fig1 <- ggplot(eff, aes(x = Water, y = est, color = Poly, shape = Poly, group = Poly)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey45", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.85, position = position_dodge(0.4)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.12, linewidth = 0.6, position = position_dodge(0.4)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, stroke = 0.6, position = position_dodge(0.4)) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_poly, labels = poly_lab, breaks = poly_levels) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = shp_poly, labels = poly_lab, breaks = poly_levels) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = water_lab_short) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6), labels = function(x) signed(x)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Effect of AMF inoculation\n(inoculated minus sterile)") +
  theme_ms(12) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0, lineheight = 1.05),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(1.1, "lines"))
print(fig1)

dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_Reversal.pdf", fig1, width = 9.5, height = 4.2)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_Reversal.png", fig1, width = 9.5, height = 4.2, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

Units: panels A and B are percent change in the response (back-transformed from the log scale);
panel C is percentage points of allocation (grain as a share of total NPP). All y-axes are free
so each panel uses its own range; the dashed line is no effect in every panel.

## Proposed caption

> **Figure 1. In monoculture, AMF inoculation turns from a grain benefit to a grain cost as
> drought intensifies; in mixed stands it has no detectable effect.** Model-estimated effect of inoculation
> (inoculated minus sterile) on (A) total productivity, (B) grain mass, and (C) grain allocation
> (grain as a share of total net primary production) at three water levels (80, 60, 40% of field
> capacity), in monoculture (orange circles) and in mixed stands with fava bean (blue triangles).
> Points are estimates from a single model per response fitted to all 60 pots; bars are 95%
> confidence intervals, unadjusted for multiplicity; the dashed line marks no effect. Every
> contrast is computed within a stand type and water level, so planting density is constant within
> each contrast and does not contribute to any estimate. n = 5 pots per cell. Panels A and B are
> percent change on the response scale (from log-scale models), panel C is percentage points.
> The confirmatory test is the three-way interaction on grain allocation (Poly x Inoc x Water,
> p = 0.00025); the contrasts plotted here are exploratory descriptions of that interaction.
> At the control water level, inoculation raised total productivity and grain mass in monoculture,
> but the allocation estimate there includes zero.

## Values plotted

```{r table}
eff %>% arrange(panel, Poly, Water) %>%
  transmute(panel, Poly, Water,
            estimate = round(est, 1), `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", lo, hi),
            `CI excludes 0` = ifelse(lo > 0 | hi < 0, "yes", "no")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Values plotted in Figure 1 (EXPLORATORY; unadjusted 95% CIs).")
```

# Companion figures (EXPLORATORY)

These raw-response figures used to be duplicated in `17_Fava_As_Treatment`; they now live only here.
All of them use one layout, set in `../fig_style.R`: monoculture panel on the left, intercrop panel on
the right; inside each panel x = water, inoculated = filled orange point and solid line, sterile = open
slate-blue point and dashed line. Points are each model's estimated means with 95% CIs (back-transformed
to the response scale).

**Letters.** Within each stand-type panel there are six cells (inoculation x water). Letters are a
Tukey-adjusted compact letter display across those six cells (15 comparisons per panel, tested on the
model's link scale): cells that share a letter are not distinguishable at alpha = 0.05. Letters are
**not** comparable between the two panels. The unadjusted inoculated vs sterile p-values that used to be
drawn are kept in a table under each figure.

```{r companion-helper}
library(multcomp)
library(multcompView)
library(car)

# Estimated means, 95% CIs, Tukey letters (within stand type) and unadjusted Inoc vs Strl p.
#   back = back-transform from the model scale (exp for the log-scale gls; identity for the beta
#          model, whose means are already put on the response scale by type = "response")
inoc_panel_stats <- function(model, back = identity) {
  emm <- emmeans(model, ~ Inoc * Water | Poly, data = wheat)
  est <- as.data.frame(summary(emm, type = "response"))
  lo <- intersect(c("asymp.LCL", "lower.CL"), names(est))[1]
  hi <- intersect(c("asymp.UCL", "upper.CL"), names(est))[1]
  yv <- intersect(c("response", "emmean"), names(est))[1]
  est <- tibble(Poly = est$Poly, Inoc = est$Inoc, Water = est$Water,
                y = back(est[[yv]]), lo = back(est[[lo]]), hi = back(est[[hi]]))
  lets <- multcomp::cld(emm, by = "Poly", adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters) %>% as.data.frame() %>%
    transmute(Poly, Inoc, Water, letter = trimws(.group))
  p_tab <- contrast(emmeans(model, ~ Inoc | Poly * Water, data = wheat), "pairwise",
                    by = c("Poly", "Water"), adjust = "none") %>% as.data.frame()
  stopifnot(all(p_tab$contrast == "Inoc - Strl"))
  est %>% left_join(lets, by = c("Poly", "Inoc", "Water")) %>%
    left_join(p_tab %>% dplyr::select(Poly, Water, p_inoc = p.value), by = c("Poly", "Water")) %>%
    mutate(Poly = poly_factor(Poly), Water = factor(Water, levels(wheat$Water)),
           Inoc = factor(Inoc, c("Inoc", "Strl")))
}

inoc_panel_fig <- function(st, ylab) {
  y_top <- max(st$hi) * 1.12
  pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.3)
  ggplot(st, aes(Water, y, group = Inoc)) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = Inoc, linetype = Inoc), linewidth = 0.8, position = pd) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, colour = Inoc), width = 0.1, linewidth = 0.6, position = pd) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = Inoc, fill = Inoc, shape = Inoc), size = 3.4, stroke = 1.1, position = pd) +
    geom_text(aes(y = hi + y_top * 0.02, label = letter, colour = Inoc), position = pd,
              size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", vjust = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
    facet_poly() + inoc_scales() +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, y_top), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_fig(12)
}

inoc_panel_table <- function(st, digits, caption) {
  st %>% arrange(Poly, Water, Inoc) %>%
    transmute(Poly, Water, Inoc, mean = round(y, digits),
              `95% CI` = sprintf(paste0("[%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]"), lo, hi),
              letter, `Inoc vs Strl p (unadj.)` = signif(p_inoc, 2)) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = caption)
}

# Inter vs Mono at each water level within each inoculation treatment (Tukey across the six
# stand type x water cells of that treatment). Moved from 17_Fava_As_Treatment.
inter_vs_mono <- function(model) {
  pairs(emmeans(model, ~ Poly * Water | Inoc, data = wheat), by = "Inoc", adjust = "tukey") %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    separate(contrast, into = c("a", "b"), sep = " - ") %>%
    separate(a, into = c("Poly_a", "Water_a"), sep = " ") %>%
    separate(b, into = c("Poly_b", "Water_b"), sep = " ") %>%
    filter(Water_a == Water_b, Poly_a != Poly_b) %>%
    transmute(Inoc, Water = factor(Water_a, levels(wheat$Water)),
              contrast = paste(Poly_a, "-", Poly_b), estimate = round(estimate, 3),
              `Tukey p` = signif(p.value, 3)) %>%
    arrange(Inoc, Water)
}
```

## Wheat NPP per pot

Wheat NPP per pot (`W_NPP`, g; the 12 or 6 wheat plants together, fava excluded). Model:
`gls(log(W_NPP) ~ Poly * Inoc * Water)` on all 60 pots with the same variance structure as panel A
(`varIdent(~ 1 | Poly)`); means are back-transformed (geometric means). **Per-pot values are not
comparable across stand types**: monoculture pots hold 12 wheat plants and intercrop pots 6, so the
intercrop panel sits lower from density alone. Only comparisons within a panel are interpretable.

```{r npp-per-pot, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6, dpi=150}
wheat$log_WNPP <- log(wheat$W_NPP)
m_wnpp <- fit_gls("log_WNPP", varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Poly))
car::Anova(m_wnpp, type = 2)
st_wnpp <- inoc_panel_stats(m_wnpp, back = exp)
fig_wnpp <- inoc_panel_fig(st_wnpp, "Wheat NPP per pot (g)")
print(fig_wnpp)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_NPP_perPot.pdf", fig_wnpp, width = 9.5, height = 6)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_NPP_perPot.png", fig_wnpp, width = 9.5, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
inoc_panel_table(st_wnpp, 1, "Wheat NPP per pot (g): geometric mean, 95% CI, Tukey letter (within stand type), unadjusted Inoc vs Strl p")
```

## Wheat BNPP per pot

Wheat belowground NPP (roots) per pot (`W_BNPP_g`, g). Model: `gls(log(W_BNPP_g) ~ Poly * Inoc * Water)`,
`varIdent(~ 1 | Poly)`, kept identical in structure to the NPP model. Same caveat: compare within a
panel only.

```{r bnpp-per-pot, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6, dpi=150}
wheat$log_WBNPP <- log(wheat$W_BNPP_g)
m_wbnpp <- fit_gls("log_WBNPP", varIdent(form = ~ 1 | Poly))
car::Anova(m_wbnpp, type = 2)
st_wbnpp <- inoc_panel_stats(m_wbnpp, back = exp)
fig_wbnpp <- inoc_panel_fig(st_wbnpp, "Wheat BNPP per pot (g)")
print(fig_wbnpp)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_BNPP_perPot.pdf", fig_wbnpp, width = 9.5, height = 6)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_BNPP_perPot.png", fig_wbnpp, width = 9.5, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
inoc_panel_table(st_wbnpp, 1, "Wheat BNPP per pot (g): geometric mean, 95% CI, Tukey letter (within stand type), unadjusted Inoc vs Strl p")
```

## Grain allocation

Wheat grain allocation (`berry_alloc` = berry / total wheat NPP, a proportion; it does not depend on
plant number, so here the two panels *are* comparable in height). Model: the beta regression used for
panel C (`m_alloc`, `dispformula = ~ Poly`); letters are tested on the logit scale, means and CIs are
back-transformed to proportions.

```{r alloc-companion, fig.width=9.5, fig.height=6, dpi=150}
car::Anova(m_alloc, type = 2)
st_alloc <- inoc_panel_stats(m_alloc)
fig_alloc <- inoc_panel_fig(st_alloc, "Grain allocation (berry / total NPP)")
print(fig_alloc)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_BerryAlloc.pdf", fig_alloc, width = 9.5, height = 6)
ggsave("figures/Fig1_BerryAlloc.png", fig_alloc, width = 9.5, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
inoc_panel_table(st_alloc, 3, "Grain allocation: model mean, 95% CI, Tukey letter (within stand type), unadjusted Inoc vs Strl p (logit scale)")
```

**Reading it.** In monoculture, inoculated and sterile wheat allocate similarly at control and moderate
water and separate sharply at severe drought; in the intercrop they do not separate at any water level.
Comparing the two panels at severe drought is the fava-suppresses-AMF-cost pattern.

## Inter vs Mono within each inoculation treatment

The fava-as-treatment view (moved from `17_Fava_As_Treatment`): at each water level, does the intercrop
differ from monoculture, separately for inoculated and sterile pots? Tukey-adjusted across the six
stand type x water cells within each inoculation treatment. Estimates are on the model scale (log for
the per-pot models, logit for allocation). **The per-pot comparisons are confounded with planting
density** (12 vs 6 wheat plants), so only the allocation table is a fair Inter vs Mono comparison.

```{r inter-vs-mono}
inter_vs_mono(m_alloc)  %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Grain allocation (logit scale): Inter vs Mono")
inter_vs_mono(m_wnpp)   %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Wheat NPP per pot (log scale): Inter vs Mono; density-confounded")
inter_vs_mono(m_wbnpp)  %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Wheat BNPP per pot (log scale): Inter vs Mono; density-confounded")
```
